 This misc.criminal case coming on for admission this day, Hon'ble
Shri Justice Dinesh Kumar Paliwal, passed the following:
 Order

This is the first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of applicants who are son and father for grant of transit anticipatory bail relating to F.I.R.No.16/2023 dated 19.01.2023 registered at P.S. Bihariganj District Madhepura (Bihar) for the offences punishable under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
2.
The facts giving rise to this case are that applicants Devendra Kumar Jain and Yogesh Jain are father and son.
Applicant Devendra Kumar is aged about 56 years and applicant Yogesh is aged about 24 years.
Applicant No.1 is businessman and is running a business of sale- purchase of food grains under the name and style of "Om Sai Ram Traders Chorai".
Complainant Ashish Kumar Choudhary also runs a business and is proprietor of "Ma Durga Trading Corporation" at District Madhepura (Bihar).
In the course of business, applicant No.1 entered into an oral agreement with the complainant to purchase Maize (corn) @ of Rs.2235 to2475/- per quintal as per the quantity of corn respectively.
The trade of 2500 quantal of maize was finalized between the parties and delivery was to be made between May, 2022 to August, 2022.

Complainant Ashish Kumar Choudhary filed a written complaint before police Bihariganj alleging that as per the agreement, he sold maize of worth Rs.1,13,30,585.50/- to the applicant but applicant paid only an amount Rs.57,00,000/- by depositing the same in his bank account.
Rest of the amount has not been paid and thus he had cheated him by not making payment of rest of the amount.
On the basis of said written complaint an offence under section 406,420 of IPC was registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that F.I.R has been lodged at police station Bihariganj District Madhepura (Bihar) while applicants are residents of District Chhindwara (M.P.).
The dispute between the parties is about transaction of maize.
It is submitted that complainant had not supplied the quality maize, therefore, he had refused to accept further consignment.
He has paid full payment to the complainant of the maize which he had received from him.
It is submitted that complainant is the resident of local police station and is an influencial person.
If applicants are not given protection, they may be arrested and some mishappening may be caused.

It is further Yogesh Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120328387/
2 submitted that they are willing to appear before the court concerned at District Madhepura (Bihar)
for the purpose of getting bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is prayed that they may be granted anticipatory transit bail for a short time so that they may appear before the competent court at Madhepura (Bihar) under limited protection granted by this court by way of time bound anticipatory transit bail.

4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by counsel for the applicant and has submitted that this court has no jurisdiction to grant any protection to the applicants as the jurisdiction lies with the High Court of Bihar.
The offence has taken place outside the state of M.P.
They may appear before the court concerned and apply for regular/ anticipatory bail.
It is submitted that present applications are not maintainable and thus prayed for rejection of the same.

5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, I am of the view that section 438 Cr.P.C specifies directions for grant of bail to a person apprehending arrest and moreover confers power only upon the High Court and the Court of Sessions to grant anticipatory or transit bail if they deem fit.
If a person has an apprehension to be arrested on an allegation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the court of Sessions for grant of anticipatory bail.
Transit anticipatory bail differs from regular/ ordinary bail.
Regular anticipatory bail is granted only in anticpation of arrest i.e it precedes detention of the accused and is effective immediately at the time of arrest.

In plain words, when an accused is arrested in accordance with the order of the court and whereas the accused needs to be tried in some other competent court having jurisdiction in the aforementioned matter, the accused is given bail for the transitory period i.e the time period required for the accused to reach that competent court from the place he is arrested.
Infact, this protection from arrest for a certain definite period is granted by the court granting such transit bail.
The grant of transit bail does not mean that the regular court under whose jurisdiction the case would fall would extend such transit bail and would convert such transit bail into anticipatory bail.
The accused person to whom transit bail has been granted has to apply for anticipatory bail before the regular court.
The regular court would consider such anticipatory bail on its own merits and shall decide such anticipatory bail application.
Thus, it can be said that transit bail is a temporary relief which an accused gets for a certain period of time so that he/she could apply for anticipatorybail before the regular court.

6. This Court in Ku. Sabinaz Vs. State of M.P. passed in M.Cr.C.No.52547/2018 vide order dated 03.01.2019 relied upon the order dated 08.02.2016 passed by the Division Bench of this court in M.Cr.C.No.269/2016 in which it is observed that "anticipatory bail can be granted in cases arising beyond the jurisdiction of the court having invested with the powers of grant of anticiatory bail.

entities.text: Ku. Sabinaz Vs. State of M.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such anticipatory bail should normally be granted only for a limited duration and the person so released be directed to approach the court within the period specified therein if he so desires and thereby the court granting anticipatory bail should leave it to the regular court to deal with the matter after expiry of the duration".

7. In the case of Teesta Atul Setalvad and another Vs. State of Maharashtra and others vide order dated 31.01.2014 passed in B.A.No.14/2014 held that "the High Court of one State can grant transit bail in respect of a case registered within the jurisdiction of another High Court in exercise of power under Section 438 of Cr.P.C."

sentences.text: From the aforesaid view taken by this Court and by Bombay High Court, it appears that there is no bar on the part of the High Court in exercising the power under section 438 of Cr.P.C in granting transit anticipatory bail for a limited period to enable the applicants to move to appropriate court as the gravity of pre-trial arrest and the loss of liberty of the individual cannot be compromised on the anvil of the powers, competence and/ or jurisdiction of the courts.

10. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case that F.I.R has been registered in a matter having a dispute about payment of money in a business transaction and applicants are apprehending their arrest in connection with F.I.R.No. 16/2023 dated 19.01.2023 registered at P.S.
Bihariganj District Madhepura (Bihar) while applicants are residents of P.S. Chourai District Chhindwara (M.P.), these applications for grant of anticipatory transit bail are allowed and it is directed that :-
(i) In the event of arrest applicants - Devendra Kumar and Yogesh Jain be released on bail on each of their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.
(ii) This anticipatory transit bail is granted only for a period of thirty days from today to enable the applicants to approach the competent court seeking appropriate relief.
(iii) Both the bail applications are allowed and disposed off accordingly.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL MANOJ KUMAR LALWANI 2023.06.21 11:17:12 +05'30'
